question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}y\,dx+x\,dy+{z}^{2}\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the helix $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+t\,k$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ]?$
question.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)=t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}y\,dx+x\,dy+{z}^{2}\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+{z}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+{z}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡t)+{t}^{2}\cdot 1\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{cos}^{2}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t+{t}^{2}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+{t}^{2}\,dt\end{aligned}
$$
